memo:
# Reading

## Compact position map

The supplied collection contains fifty-eight held texts, all assessable through checked profiles; *Marx’s First Model of the Transition to Capitalism* is additionally held in full. The map below is compact because the oeuvre divides into several concurrent argumentative routes rather than one linear sequence.

- **Historical formation, 1972–78.** em:VAYFENVQ/1972, *The Social Basis of English Commercial Expansion, 1550–1650*, makes socially constituted merchant groups mediate commercial opportunities; em:27CQX9UR/1976, *Agrarian Class Structure and Economic Development in Pre-Industrial Europe*, makes class power and property relations mediate demographic and commercial pressures; em:HZHLWZ2R/1977, *The Origins of Capitalist Development*, distinguishes capitalist compulsion from exchange and places divergent class conflict at the centre of transition; em:9VI9FSBK/1978, *Reply to Sweezy*, identifies the unexplained conditions and uneven success of primitive accumulation. Their qualification is decisive: they establish the focal text’s positive causal commitments before its Marxological reconstruction [E1.F1–E1.F5; E2.F1–E2.F3].

- **Independent political route, 1980–84.** em:BHRWPT7F/1980, *A New Social Democracy?*; em:TGWH6ZPU/1981, *Reagan, the Right and the Working Class*; em:6U35NCDN/1981, *The Right Wing and the Working Class: A Response*; em:Q6WXW5PM/1983, *Again on Reform or Revolution in Poland*; and em:SS9844LV/1984, *Can the Left Use the Democratic Party?*, argue that material structures become politically effective through organization, practical strategies, struggle, and independent mass activity. This is compatible with, but not derived from, the focal transition argument [E1.F6–E1.F7].

- **The 1985–93 hinge and branching.** em:CBT7B8CL/1985, *Marx’s First Model of the Transition to Capitalism*, reconstructs two incompatible historical materialisms; em:9RJCZ6KQ/1985, *The Agrarian Roots of European Capitalism*, supplies the same year’s broad comparative history; em:HYA4MA32/1985, *The Paradox of Social Democracy*, continues the political route. em:3JSL5XP4/1986, *Austerity & Interventionism*; em:S52G8SSP/1986, *The Deep Roots of U.S. Economic Decline*; em:KUF7CP3S/1986, *The Elections and the Left*; and em:XTTG43Z5/1986, *The Social Basis of Economic Development*, respectively develop political economy, electoral strategy, and the formal property–reproduction chain. em:3PBW7WA9/1988, *Notes on the Crash and Crisis*, begins the profitability route; em:LJFTS6KY/1989, *Bourgeois Revolution and Transition to Capitalism*, directly resumes the focal reconstruction; em:2VPKTHSN/1989, the Soviet contribution, transfers class-property analysis to bureaucratic collectivism. The 1991 Soviet essays em:GR426WC5 and em:IMRP3JQ7 extend that transfer; em:D28G2RWK/1991 attacks institutional primacy; em:K67KNHJC/1991 explains counterproductive imperial policy. em:8X5QYXZG/1993 and em:ZJHK954P/1993 analyse state constraint and reformism, while em:ZH86SA7Z/1993, *Merchants and Revolution*, greatly enlarges the 1972 historical route. The qualification is that these are multiple branches, not one post-1985 programme caused by the focal text [E2.F1–E2.F5].

- **Mature political economy and historical synthesis, 1995–2011.** em:U42IYG2I/1995 links profitability decline to political realignment. em:BD8RCVGB/1998 continues rank-and-file politics, while em:ZFPK9NTQ/1998, em:L7CX4T2I/1998, em:4DYCDX3A/1999, and em:A5KQX6MT/1999 construct the mature account of competition, fixed capital, overcapacity, and failed adjustment. em:T33SBUEY/2000 and em:TAGBBUU9/2001 distinguish real recovery from bubble dependence. em:ATQRKQMC/2001 provides a historical mechanism for unintended transition. The five 2002 economic texts—em:F4ET2EQE, em:KFEA7SRZ, em:TJJZHZ6J, em:TP2BBTZI, em:CB8B4RIL—apply or test the crisis theory; em:UYYQABRK/2002 globalizes the transition comparison. em:FDEWCETE/2004 qualifies earlier electoral abstention with tactical critical support, while em:DXBHHXIJ/2004 continues the bubble diagnosis. em:BHSWIJKN/2005 and em:QP74AWIU/2006 consolidate the long-downturn account; em:PWVE5QPN/2006 synthesizes transition; em:BJ4R4EPJ/2006 extends unintended interaction to the multiple-state system. em:C3E3GHEL/2007 formalizes the mature transition chain; em:UFFBTFJW/2007 connects accumulation to political realignment; em:32EZD9WF/2009 applies the crisis account to finance; em:WNQLQHP7/2010 rejoins profitability analysis to labour history; em:S8AUYJ5G/2011 and em:C8KU3XVS/2011 synthesize feudalism and preindustrial non-development. The major qualification is that the crisis route assigns immediate causal priority to competition among capitals rather than class struggle.

- **Late political-economic reorientation, 2017–25.** em:7QSF5QUB/2017, *Introducing Catalyst*, joins long-downturn economics to organized socialist politics; em:NE7AJREG/2020, *Escalating Plunder*, identifies politically enabled predation; em:2887CIMF/2021, *From Theory to History*, restates the merged political economy of feudalism against Mann; em:V68V5D49/2022 and em:VE9TU4JA/2025 theorize political capitalism and an asset circuit alongside productive accumulation. This is a later reorientation, not one inaugurated by the focal paper.

No ordering is inferred among texts sharing a year. The packet establishes publication or edition years, not composition sequence. The sample is also not the complete oeuvre: the prior analysis reports twelve listed but unsupplied works, so absence here cannot establish disappearance from Brenner’s work as a whole [E4.F1–E4.F3].

## The paper read backwards: what it culminates

Read backwards, em:CBT7B8CL/1985 culminates the 1972–78 formation of a class-relational account rather than founding it. The 1976 article had already argued that property relations impose “specific long-term patterns” on development; the focal text recasts that causal ontology as a contrast between two Marxisms, defining the later one through social-property relations that structure reproduction. Its object is therefore not newly discovered class causation. Its distinctive act is **theoretical self-clarification**: it turns the earlier rejection of demographic and commercial automatism into an internal reconstruction of Marx.

The continuity is particularly strong on transition. The 1977 article had already denied that trade could transform class relations, while the 1978 reply asked what conditions made primitive accumulation succeed unevenly. The focal text sharpens this into the question of how feudal actors, reproducing themselves feudally, transform feudal property relations. Thus its retrospective status is **culmination**: it codifies and discriminates between the premises already operating in the earlier historical argument.

The qualification is methodological. Earlier texts mainly compare historical outcomes or criticize trade-centred explanations; the focal paper instead reads Marx’s early and later works against one another. Its claim that there are “two fundamentally different historical materialisms” makes this a genuine reorientation in argumentative route, though not a rupture in causal ontology.

## The paper read forwards: what it seeds

Read forwards, the paper is a **way station**, not the unique origin of the mature framework. Its most direct sequel is em:LJFTS6KY/1989, *Bourgeois Revolution and Transition to Capitalism*, which resumes the two-model distinction and applies it to the English Revolution: the textual reconstruction becomes a historical reinterpretation of agrarian capitalism and the “landlord shell”.

Its most important prospective achievement is to pose, rather than solve, the mechanism of endogenous transition. em:ATQRKQMC/2001 answers in general form that capitalist social-property relations emerged from feudal actors carrying out feudal rules for reproduction; em:PWVE5QPN/2006 and em:C3E3GHEL/2007 repeat and systematize that answer [F5–F6]. These later texts do not merely repeat the focal paper’s vocabulary: they change its inferential role. What is an announced historical task in 1985 becomes a positive causal proposition and then a formal chain from property relations through reproductive rules to aggregate development and crisis.

The same relational grammar travels beyond transition history. The Soviet writings explain economic dynamics through class-property relations; the mature crisis writings explain how individually compulsory cost-cutting reproduces aggregate overcapacity and low profitability [F7–F8]. This is best treated as a **transfer or reargument**, not proof of direct inheritance: the objects differ, and most later crisis texts do not reproduce the focal article’s genealogy of early Marx.

The focal route also becomes less central than its positive framework. Later transition syntheses retain social-property relations, market dependence, rules for reproduction, and unintended consequences, but the extended discussion of individuation, communal property, and craft–manufacture–machinofacture largely recedes. Accordingly, the focal text seeds a durable problem and conceptual grammar, but its distinctive Marxological apparatus has selective uptake.

## The paper read whole: the joined verdict

Read whole, em:CBT7B8CL/1985 is a **middle-period reorientation and deepening**: retrospectively a culmination of the 1972–78 class-relational transition argument; prospectively a way station toward explicit rules-for-reproduction and unintended-transition accounts; and, as a rupture verdict, a reorientation in method rather than a break in substantive theory.

What **persists** is the claim that neither trade, technology, demography, institutions, nor opportunities determine development independently of historically formed social-property relations and the strategies those relations make rational. What **breaks** at the focal text is the immediate evidentiary route: comparative history and contemporary controversy give way to internal reconstruction of two Marxian historical materialisms [F1–F3].

What changes later is not attributable to 1985 alone. Crisis theory makes inter-capitalist competition the immediate mechanism of recession and recovery, creating tension with the focal paper’s call for a deepened appreciation of class formation and class struggle. Still later, political capitalism gives state-backed rents and asset appreciation greater conceptual autonomy, while explicitly placing the new circuit alongside rather than in place of productive capitalism. Those are stronger later revisions than anything occurring at the focal boundary.

The collection’s overall position is therefore: **formation before 1985; codification, historical specification, and transfer after it; late reorientation toward political capitalism**. The focal paper is the hinge at which an existing historical programme becomes self-conscious about its Marxological alternatives and states its hardest unresolved question.

## Reading route

1. **em:HZHLWZ2R/1977, *The Origins of Capitalist Development: A Critique of Neo-Smithian Marxism*.** Read first to see that the anti-commercialization thesis, class-conflict account, and distinction between market exchange and capitalist compulsion predate the focal paper.

2. **em:27CQX9UR/1976, *Agrarian Class Structure and Economic Development in Pre-Industrial Europe*.** Read second for the comparative historical foundation: property relations mediate common demographic and commercial pressures into divergent outcomes.

3. **em:LJFTS6KY/1989, *Bourgeois Revolution and Transition to Capitalism*.** Read third because it is the clearest direct sequel, carrying the two-model reconstruction into interpretation of the English Revolution.

4. **em:ATQRKQMC/2001, *The Low Countries in the Transition to Capitalism*.** Read fourth because it converts the focal paper’s unanswered question into a historical mechanism of unintended transformation through feudal rules for reproduction.

5. **em:C3E3GHEL/2007, *Property and Progress: Where Adam Smith Went Wrong*.** Read fifth for the mature systematization of the framework as a causal chain from social-property relations to strategies, aggregate patterns, and crises.

## Open question

The chief unresolved issue is whether em:CBT7B8CL/1985 was the beginning of a sustained Marxological project or a specialized first instalment whose positive framework was developed mainly elsewhere. The text calls itself “Part I of a longer work,” but the supplied collection identifies no certain completion. Locating that continuation would decide whether the paper is merely a hinge within the transition oeuvre or the surviving opening of a larger, partly missing reconstruction.

A second uncertainty is chronological: the packet cannot establish whether the focal article, same-year *Agrarian Roots*, and the 1986 *Social Basis* were composed sequentially or in parallel. Composition histories, drafts, or correspondence would be needed before claiming that the focal paper generated the “rules for reproduction” formulation.

agendas.text: Commercial opportunities have socially variable effects and are partly constituted by merchant capacities
agendas.anchor: The reaction to commercial opportunity (or cost), if indeed there is one, will tend to vary with the social, political, and economic character of the mercantile group.

agendas.text: The comparative agrarian agenda asks how class relations mediate demographic and commercial change
agendas.anchor: It is the structure of class relations, of class power, which will determine the manner and degree to which particular demographic and commercial changes will affect long-run trends in the distribution of income and economic growth — and not vice versa.

agendas.text: The transition agenda rejects trade as a sufficient cause because trade cannot itself transform class relations
agendas.anchor: The rise of trade is not at the origin of a dynamic of development because trade cannot determine the transformation of class relations of production.

agendas.text: The 1986 theory generalizes the property-relations model into rules of reproduction and compulsory specialization
agendas.anchor: form of property relations—rules for reproduction of the individual economic actors>long-term pattern of economic development/non-development.

agendas.text: Merchant history develops from socially constituted commercial opportunity into an account of merchant blocs and political power
agendas.anchor: Rather than responding to crisis imperatives, they were exploiting special opportunities which they themselves had created.

agendas.text: The reformism agenda treats social democracy as limiting struggle and requires organization outside it
agendas.anchor: the overriding tendency within social democracy has been not only to relinquish socialism as a goal and revolution as a means, but to set strict limits to working class struggle and the development of working class politics

agendas.text: The mature social-democracy argument says official reformism undermines its own mass basis
agendas.anchor: The paradoxical consequence has been that, to the extent that the official representatives of reformism in general and social democratic parties in particular have been freed to implement their characteristic worldviews, strategies, and tactics, they have systematically undermined the basis for their own continuing existence.

agendas.text: The long-downturn agenda makes competition-generated overcapacity the central cause of falling profitability
agendas.anchor: It is the logic of competition, not class struggle, that rules the deeper rhythms of growth or recession.

agendas.text: Capitalist social-property relations remain the background constraint against institution-centered explanations
agendas.anchor: The general weakness of Regulation Theory, paradoxical though this may seem, is its failure to take adequately into account the broader system of capitalist social-property relations that forms the backdrop to their succession of institutionally defined phases.

agendas.text: The 2006 synthesis makes individual competitive responses reproduce aggregate stagnation
agendas.anchor: The economy enters the downturn, then, because the measures that individual economic actors are obliged to take to counteract their own reduced profitability serve to reproduce the problem of reduced profitability at the aggregate level.

agendas.text: Bubble analysis distinguishes real profitability recovery from debt- and asset-driven prolongation
agendas.anchor: The Boom opened the way to the Bubble, but the Bubble has blown up the Boom a good deal more.

agendas.text: The financial-crisis account treats finance as an amplifier of long-term weakness and asset-price Keynesianism
agendas.anchor: The fundamental source of today’s crisis is the steadily declining vitality of the advanced capitalist economies over three decades, business-cycle by business-cycle, right into the present.

agendas.text: The American-politics agenda explains rightward movement through real material pressures and weakened class struggle
agendas.anchor: Workers have moved right instead of left because of what they perceive to be—and what in a limited but important sense really are—their immediate, short-run economic interests

agendas.text: The bureaucratic-society agenda identifies a state-organized ruling class extracting surplus through political exclusion
agendas.anchor: We have a bureaucratic ruling class collectively organised in a state, politically excluding the workers in order to take a surplus

agendas.text: The latest text preserves the profitability-centered downturn while adding a rent-oriented political circuit
agendas.anchor: Our central contention was that the post-war macro-economy experienced a two-phased evolution—long boom followed by long downturn—and that this was paralleled by the two-phased evolution of the profit rate.

turns.text: The 1984 polemic sharply separates electoral and mass-action logics
turns.anchor: There is a strict logic to winning elections which is quite different from the logic of winning strikes or organizing successful mass militant actions of any sort.

turns.text: Electoral tactics are later qualified by critical support, while strategic independence persists
turns.anchor-c: "The Democratic Party has been a graveyard for progressive mass movements"
turns.anchor: Those leftists who intend to use the Democratic Party in general and the electoral struggle in particular for the goals of the left drastically underestimate the barriers to doing so.

turns.text: The economic agenda turns from U.S. manufacturing decline to a general theory of the long downturn
turns.anchor: the key to the distinctive trajectory of U.S. politics in the later 1970s and 1980s is to be found in the long-term relative decline of both the competitiveness of U.S. manufacturing and the attractiveness of U.S. manufacturing as a field for investment.

turns.text: Political capitalism reorients the long-downturn agenda toward state-mediated returns without positing a new mode of production
turns.anchor: Under political capitalism, raw political power, rather than productive investment, is the key determinant of the rate of return.

turns.text: The Soviet agenda turns from classifying bureaucratic rule to explaining the crisis of partial marketization
turns.anchor: Class structure is the key to society’s economic dynamic, its laws of motion and forms of crisis.

place.text: The focal text’s positive model makes transition the transformation of feudal property relations through feudal actors’ reproduction
place.anchor: The model's ultimate objective is to explain “the so-called primitive accumulation" - which, from this standpoint, refers to the — series of societal processes by which the fundamental property relationships which constitute the feudal mode of production are broken up and transformed through the action of feudal society itself.

place.text: The 1989 return confirms that the focal distinction became a framework for reinterpreting bourgeois revolution
place.anchor-c: "It must, at every strategic juncture, assume the transition in order to explain the transition."
place.anchor: It was the problem of accounting for the transformation of pre-capitalist property relations into capitalist property relations via the action of pre-capitalist society itself.

place.text: Later transition histories presuppose the focal text’s unintended-consequence formulation
place.anchor: the emergence of capitalist social-property relations had to result from attempts by feudal individual actors to carry out feudal rules for reproduction

place.text: The 2007 synthesis converts the focal distinction into a general causal chain
place.anchor: The causal chain runs from historically specific, politically reproduced social property relations to individual rules for reproduction to aggregate developmental patterns to society-wide forms of crisis.

retrospective.text: The focal text explains why the 1977 rejection of trade-led transition follows logically: regular innovation and competitive selection require already-capitalist market dependence
retrospective.answer: its systematic developmental mechanism presupposes competitive production for exchange
retrospective.anchor: Under such already-capitalist conditions, we can be fairly sure that the progression laid out by Marx actually will occur.

retrospective.text: The focal text answers the 1978 demand to specify primitive accumulation by defining its result as the dissolution of pre-capitalist reproduction and the compulsion to exchange
retrospective.tension: conditions and content of primitive accumulation were unspecified
retrospective.answer: producers are separated from their means of reproduction and must exchange to survive
retrospective.left_open: why that separation succeeds in some cases
retrospective.anchor: the direct producers are not only entirely free to produce for exchange, but must in fact exchange in order to survive.

retrospective.text: The focal text sharpens rather than solves the positive historical problem: how feudal reproduction generates transformation
retrospective.tension: class conflict must explain geographically uneven transition
retrospective.answer: transition must be traced through lords’ and peasants’ attempts to reproduce themselves as feudal classes
retrospective.left_open: the mechanism and outcome of those struggles
retrospective.anchor: To confront this problem - which Marx barely posed and never solved - will require in my opinion, a deepened appreciation of the role of class formation and class struggle

retrospective.text: Marx is an inherited interlocutor, but the focal text divides his work: it disputes the early model and builds on the later property-relations model
retrospective.anchor: Nevertheless, by the end of the 1850s, Marx had provided the basis for quite a different historical materialism, precisely by refining his understanding of property relations

retrospective.text: Adam Smith is inherited but changes role from external model of trade-led development to the genealogy of Marx’s first model
retrospective.anchor: Specifically, it mirrors rather closely Adam Smith's classic account of the © transition from feudalism to capitalism in the Wealth of Nations

retrospective.text: The focal text inherits the earlier demand for autonomous class conflict and argues that early Marx deprives struggle of causal efficacy by predetermining its outcomes through productive-force development
retrospective.what: causal autonomy of class formation and struggle
retrospective.done_with_it: turns it into the criterion distinguishing the two models
retrospective.anchor: the outcomes of these class struggles cannot affect the supercession of one stage by the next; for they are themselves predetermined by the development of the productive forces.

retrospective.text: Pre-capitalist possession resolves why innovation need not spread despite exchange: producers not dependent on markets need not follow competitors to survive
retrospective.tension: similar commercial pressures yielded different outcomes in 1976
retrospective.answer: direct access to reproduction blocks compulsory competitive selection
retrospective.left_open: why possession is maintained or destroyed
retrospective.anchor: they are not necessarily obliged to follow, since they do not produce for exchange and so do not have to compete on the market to survive.

retrospective.text: The focal text qualifies its reconstruction as retrospective rather than presenting the early-to-late contrast as a contemporaneously explicit development
retrospective.anchor: This section is, frankly, based on “hindsight”. That is, — it employs conceptions of Marx's later works to interrogate his earlier works

retrospective.text: The later property model replaces automatic dissolution by trade with a new collective-action problem concerning transformation among actors committed to reproducing existing relations
retrospective.anchor: In providing reasons to foresake the invisible hand, Marx obliges himself to confront a whole series of prisoners dilemmas.

retrospective.text: Engels, Sweezy, and Wallerstein are inherited interlocutors treated as later adopters of the Smithian strategy made available by early Marx
retrospective.anchor: any number of Marxists, from Engels to Sweezy to Wallerstein, would \"follow\" the master in adopting essentially Smithian strategies to explain large-scale historical transformations

retrospective.text: North and Thomas are inherited as a qualified analogy between early Marx’s adaptive property forms and the property-rights school
retrospective.anchor: it does not appear to distinguish itself, in qualitative terms, from the “historical” processes envisioned by today's “property rights school” of economics and economic history

retrospective.text: G. A. Cohen is a new interlocutor in the supplied pre-focal collection, mentioned as offering functionalism as an alternative route to productive-force primacy
retrospective.anchor: For an attempt to provide an alternative strategy to the same end through the use of functionalist explanation, see G.A. Cohen, Karl Marx's Theory of History: A Defence, Princeton, 1979.

retrospective.text: The focal text is a culmination of the supplied transition agenda because it converts the earlier anti-commercialization thesis into an internal reconstruction of two incompatible historical materialisms, while leaving the positive transition mechanism unresolved
retrospective.warrant: it explains the conceptual source and circularity of the trade-centred model and specifies property transformation as the proper problem
retrospective.of_agenda: the 1972–78 transition and anti-economic-determinist agenda, not the independent 1980–84 political route
retrospective.anchor: Correlatively, I will attempt to show that precisely by basing his second model of the rise of capitalism in his mode of production concept, Marx enables us to pose the problem of transition

prospective.text: The focal text distinguishes two incompatible historical materialisms, making their contrast the starting point for the later agenda
prospective.how: applied to bourgeois revolution and English capitalism
prospective.anchor: There are two Marxian models of the transition from feudalism to capitalism. These are often confused and run_ together. Nevertheless, they are entirely incompatible

prospective.text: The focal text makes social-property relations the structures that enable and organize societal reproduction
prospective.what: mode of production as reproductive property structure
prospective.how: reformulated as rules for reproduction producing development or non-development
prospective.anchor: Its master principle is the mode of production, conceived as a system of social Property relations which make possible, and thereby structure, Societal reproduction

prospective.text: The focal text poses but does not solve how feudal actors transform the relations they seek to reproduce
prospective.how: identified as the emergence of capitalism from attempts to follow feudal rules
prospective.anchor: To confront this problel - which Marx barely posed and never solved - will require in my opinion, a deepened appreciation of the role of clas: formation and class struggle

prospective.anchor: social-property systems, once established, tend to set strict limits and impose certain overall patterns upon the course of economic evolution.

prospective.text: *The Social Basis of Economic Development* adopts the focal property/reproduction alternative while abstracting from its full Marxological reconstruction

prospective.anchor: form of property relations—rules for reproduction of the individual economic actors>long-term pattern of economic development/non-development.

prospective.text: The unresolved transition question becomes a general unintended-consequences thesis

prospective.anchor: It was the problem of accounting for the transformation of pre-capitalist property relations into capitalist property relations via the action of pre-capitalist society itself.

prospective.text: *The Low Countries* operationalizes the focal framework through regional comparison and supplies an unintended-consequences mechanism
prospective.warrant: it turns the open theoretical problem into a historical explanation

prospective.text: The focal distinction between possession and market dependence becomes a comparative explanation of English–Yangzi divergence
prospective.what: competitive constraint created by separation from subsistence
prospective.how: used to explain divergent resource allocation and productivity paths
prospective.anchor: they are not necessarily obliged to follow, since they do not produce for exchange and so do not have to compete on the market to survive.

prospective.text: *Property and Progress* consolidates the focal alternative into an explicit multi-level causal chain

prospective.anchor: The causal chain runs from historically specific, politically reproduced social property relations to individual rules for reproduction to aggregate developmental patterns to society-wide forms of crisis.

prospective.text: Compulsory market dependence is later developed into the general foundation of capitalist accumulation and competition
prospective.how: competition becomes the condition of enterprise survival and cost cutting
prospective.anchor: everyone must buy most of what they need. In order to buy what they need, they must not only have something they} can sell, but actually be able to sell it \"on the market\

prospective.text: The focal prisoners-dilemma problem is transferred from transition to capitalist crisis: compelled individual remedies reproduce aggregate failure
prospective.what: unintended aggregate consequences of reproductive action
prospective.how: firms’ defensive responses reproduce reduced profitability
prospective.anchor: In providing reasons to foresake the invisible hand, Marx obliges himself to confront a whole series of prisoners dilemmas.

prospective.text: The same causal paradox remains explicit in the 2025 account of secular stagnation
prospective.what: capitalist dynamism as source of stagnation
prospective.how: investment compelled by competition both develops production and depresses returns
prospective.anchor: There is no mechanism of natural selection weeding out those who fail to produce at _ the “socially necessary\" rate.

prospective.text: The relation between possession and extra-economic coercion is generalized to Soviet bureaucratic collectivism
prospective.what: political surplus extraction where producers are not market-dependent
prospective.how: the ruling class is defined by collective state organization and forced appropriation
prospective.anchor: since in all pre-capitalist economies, the direct producers possess their means of reproduction, any ruling class can reproduce itself only by establishing and maintaining its domination

prospective.text: The focal account of feudal coercion matures into an integrated conception of feudal class, state and political economy
prospective.what: merger of property, coercion and political organization
prospective.how: used to criticize separation of economic and political power
prospective.anchor: a class of lordly rulers and exploiters, who reproduce themselves by extracting a surplus from the peasant producers by means of extra-economic compulsion.

prospective.text: The political writings preserve a relational, anti-automatic method but do not demonstrate uptake of the focal text as a whole
prospective.warrant: outcomes depend on organized action and institutional position rather than conditions alone
prospective.anchor: The isolation of these movements, the flip side of their autonomy, proved their undoing.

prospective.text: The extended genealogy of individuation from tribal communal property is not returned to as a major explanatory object in the supplied later corpus
prospective.what: progressive individuation from tribe to private property
prospective.anchor: In broadest terms, then, Marx sketches a process of individuation leading from tribal-communal property toward capitalism by way of exchange and specialization.

prospective.text: The detailed craft–manufacture–machinofacture stage sequence is not subsequently developed in the supplied texts
prospective.anchor: Craft production was superseded by manufacturing productior which gave rise to industrial production.

prospective.text: The family as the ultimate social atom of mechanical individualism disappears from the later supplied framework
prospective.anchor: A premise of all social-historical development, it is the ultimate social atom.

prospective.text: The promised full continuation of the two-model reconstruction is not identifiable in the supplied corpus
prospective.anchor: This article is Part I of a longer work to be published separately.

prospective.text: The focal text is the origin of the supplied later social-property/reproduction agenda because later texts repeatedly operationalize its open problem across transition history, comparative development and capitalist crisis

prospective.of_agenda: social-property relations, rules for reproduction, unintended transition and aggregate contradictions

rupture.text: The 1972 text already rejects automatic market causation by making responses to opportunity vary with the constitution of merchant groups
rupture.anchor: The reaction to commercial opportunity (or cost), if indeed there is one, will tend to vary with the social, political, and economic character of the mercantile group.

rupture.text: The 1976 text already places class relations between demographic-commercial causes and long-run outcomes
rupture.anchor: It is the structure of class relations, of class power, which will determine the manner and degree to which particular demographic and commercial changes will affect long-run trends in the distribution of income and economic growth — and not vice versa.

rupture.text: The 1977 text already rejects trade as the origin of capitalist development because trade cannot transform class relations
rupture.anchor: The rise of trade is not at the origin of a dynamic of development because trade cannot determine the transformation of class relations of production.

rupture.text: The 1978 reply already identifies the missing explanatory role of relatively autonomous class development and conflict
rupture.anchor: The place of relatively autonomous, ‘discontinuous’ processes of class development and class conflict was not made clear; or it appeared to be strictly subordinated to—the necessary effect of—the growth of trade.

rupture.text: Before the focal text, the political route also rejects automatic effects of worsening conditions and explains conduct through materially situated practical strategies
rupture.anchor: significant sections of the working class have become open to right wing political ideas in response to very real conditions and very difficult problems.
